findings.authorizedBy: R-PUNCT-STRUCT, applied by the prior pass.
findings.diagnosis: As punctuation the colon is defensible: an effort to help specifies what reverent humility is here. But the sentence is presented as a quotation of Volume I, and Volume I's current canonical text renders the same span with a comma. The punctuation standard forbids silently altering an exact quotation to satisfy the glyph rule; the honest treatments are matching the source or obtaining approval for the adaptation. Because CTD-0007 leaves verbatim-versus-adaptation to the author, the colon is left standing rather than silently retuned a second time, and the one-mark divergence is put in front of the author in Q1.

Italicizing the attribution removes the glyph without inventing punctuation, and the same treatment is applied to all nine epigraph attributions in the volume, so the form is consistent. Correct repair, recorded as examined; the volume-wide count belongs to the epigraph refrain noted in the chapter-one record's audit.
